task.description: Step 3b of WF-02 for REQ-007. Read docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-007.md directly. Verify every one of REQ-007's 5 acceptance criteria has a precise, runnable case with no coverage gaps. Verify no case requires a judgment call TEST-RUNNER can't make mechanically. acceptance_criteria: Every AC has a corresponding case, checked individually
Every case's expected output is precise enough to pass/fail without judgment
AC4's embedded expected numbers independently re-verified against a live run

result.summary: Read docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-007.md directly (not TEST-DESIGNER's summary). Confirmed all 5 of REQ-007's acceptance criteria (verified verbatim against docs/agents/requirements.yaml) map 1:1 to a dedicated case (AC1-AC5), each with an exact command/route and a literal expected output (exact file lists, exact exit codes, exact 'error TS'/'Cannot find module' absence checks, exact <html lang> values, exact HTTP 200, exact commit-message substrings) -- no case relies on 'looks right' or unstated judgment. Grepped for 'TODO' and vagueness phrases ('looks right', 'should work', 'as expected'): the only match is the spec's own closing disclaimer stating it avoided such language, not an instance of it. Independently re-ran AC4's key-set diff script myself (not trusted from the spec): `ls apps/web/messages/` returned exactly en.json, kk.json, ru.json, uz.json, and the Node leaves()-diff script produced ru_count=177, uz_count=177 missing=[] extra=[], en_count=177 missing=[] extra=[], kk_count=177 missing=[] extra=[] -- matches the spec's embedded expected output exactly, character for character.
